title: A split simplicial module has the homotopy type of its nondegenerate complex
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $U$ a simplicial $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Suppose given modules $V_n$, inclusions $j_n:V_n\to U_n$, and, in every degree $n\geq0$, a direct-sum decomposition
$$\bigoplus_{\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[k]}V_k\xrightarrow{\sim}U_n,$$
whose summand map is $U(\theta)j_k$, where the sum ranges over order-preserving surjections and all $0\leq k\leq n$. Let $\pi_n:U_n\to V_n$ be the projection onto the identity-surjection summand. Let $C(U)_n=U_n$ with differential $\partial_n=\sum_{a=0}^n(-1)^ad_a$ for $n>0$, and zero out of degree zero. Put $V_n=0$ for $n<0$. Then $V$ with differential $\partial^V_n=\pi_{n-1}\partial_nj_n$ is a chain complex, and there are chain maps $f:C(U)\to V$, $g:V\to C(U)$ such that $gf$ and $fg$ are chain homotopic to their respective identity maps. A chain homotopy means degree-one $R$-linear maps $H_n$ with the difference of the two maps equal to $\partial H+H\partial$.
